# 1 Clement Chapter 23 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 23 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_023_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 23

**23:1** The compassionate Father, rich in mercy, has compassion on those who fear him, graciously and kindly bestowing his favors on all who come to him with sincerity of heart.

**23:2** Let us therefore not be wavering in mind, nor let our soul entertain vain imaginings concerning his surpassing and glorious gifts.

**23:3** Let that scripture be far from us which says: "Miserable are the double-minded, those who doubt in their soul, saying: 'We heard these things in our fathers' time too, and look—we have grown old, and not one of these things has come to pass for us.'"

**23:4** O you foolish ones! Compare your lot to that of a tree: take a vine. First it loses its leaves, then a bud forms, then a leaf appears, then a flower, and after this an unripe grape, then a full cluster of ripe grapes. You see that in a little while the fruit of the tree reaches maturity.

**23:5** Truly, quickly and suddenly his will shall be accomplished; and scripture itself testifies: "He will come and will not delay; and the Lord will come suddenly into his temple, the Holy One whom you expect."

---

*LOGOS renders with formal equivalence, preserving rhetorical structure and the extended vine analogy.*
